description: Making a Mars mission outpost simulation with mission objectives such as collecting samples, exploring, and navigating through challanges like solar storms, radiation warnings, and more.
summary: We made a Mars outpost mission simulation, addressing the challenge of teaching kids the variables and challenges in running and managing an outpost while executing a 365-day mission on Mars. Our game, Martianers, teaches how to navigate through emergencies like dust storms, radiation warnings, emergency oxygen shortages, water shortages, limited food supplies, and more. Our game includes a navigation map for which players can explore the map and potentially find lost NASA rovers, come across past rover landing sites, read fun facts when relevant to the situation in game, complete mission objectives such as collecting samples and inspecting them, have rovers and drones accompany them on expeditions, and look through rock samples from past rovers through AI-powered computers, as well as ask preset questions and communicate to Earth 24/7. All of these are important to teach kids a lesson in management, critical decision-making, analyzing, and prioritization in the context of potential future space missions. We aim to bring back kids' love and curiosity for science, exploration, and engineering.
details:
The game begins with a cutscene upon arrival. It starts off with a view of Mars from outer space, in a spaceship, approaching Mars. The spaceship descends, and a robot named 'Marv' is nearby, watching excitedly. Player puts on spacesuit, and steps out of the space cabin. Player is greeted by Merv, and is then toured around the already set up outpost (with resources, habitats and supplies sent months before the manned mission, along with robots to check that everything's set and ready). The first mission objective is to tour around the place, with Marv. There's a checklist for each room to explore.

After the first mission objective is completed, players unlock access the rovers and drones garage. In Martianers, everytime a player completes a mission objective, they obtain an award--whether through an outpost expansion, an upgrade, or extra resources and supplies.

Players would then have several missions, involving:
- Exploring and collecting samples
- Searching for lost rovers
- Coming across past rover landing sites, for which there'll be a fun fact sliding out on the bottom right, with information about the rover.
- Managing water supply, oxygen supply, food supply, and greenhouse mechanics.

Players would have a few challenges to navigate:
- Dust storms and radiation warnings, where player must retreat from mission and seek shelter/protected area.
- Conditions where players have to choose between actions, while considering its consequences. For example:
Water supply is running low. Players could choose to:
a. Postpone the mission and focus on managing the outpost
b. Inspect the water supply and have the possibility of finding a malfunction and fixing it
c. Proceed with mission anyway, conserving as much water as possible.
- Emergencies such as oxygen depletion/running low on oxygen, where players will have to decide whether to continue on route, or retreat and return the next day.

Habitats are built inspired by real NASA experiments and future tools, such as CHAPEA (inspiration for the living quarters), MOXIE (for oxygen supply), EVA suits, greenhouse mechanics, fission power units, and more.

Data on Mars Atmosphere is based off real data from Perseverance's MEDA sensors.
Mars terrain is based on DEM files on Mars Trek, around the Jezero Crater (player's landing site and outpost location).

Our project is creative because we've added Marv, a friendly, funny, cheerful and curious robot mascot that'll guide the player, provide context, and push the player towards findings by saying things like "HUMAN HUMAN LOOK!!!"

We've also added fun facts and information about the player's surroundings, teaching kids about real NASA findings, and ongoing developments.

To execute and bring our ideas to life, we used Codex to code and design models and scenes on Blender and Godot. We also used ChatGPT image generator to quickly map and picture our ideas regardning blueprints and room designs.

Gemini AI was used to sort and organize MEDA data.

We intend for this project to teach kids a lot about Mars, ongoing space research, and train their thinking skills in a fun, engaging way. We hope that this can make kids fall in love with the frontiers of human discovery (space science) once again, as the future generation and hope of humanity.
